chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah or Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who had ten slave girls, so he did Zahaar from all of them together by one speech. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him are ten expiations.'

key_terms.فَظَاهَرَ: He performed Zahaar (the act of likening the wife to the mother, requiring expiation)

ai.seo_question: How many expiations are required for Zahaar if done for multiple women in one speech?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of individuality in expiation (kaffarat), establishing that each wife constitutes a distinct legal entity requiring a separate atonement even when the declaration is made simultaneously. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the multiplicity of obligations corresponding to the number of subjects, distinguishing it from cases where a single act might suffice for multiple parties. The hadith serves as a foundational precedent for calculating financial and ritual liabilities in family law.
